one_liner: Pure-Rust regex engine with lookarounds, backreferences and an x86-64/AArch64 JIT; claims up to 4x over the regex crate.
what_it_does: A regex crate written for LLM tokenizer split patterns (cl100k_base, Llama 3) that need lookarounds, which the regex crate omits, without linking libpcre2. The API mirrors the regex crate (Regex::new, is_match, find, find_iter, captures, captures_iter, replace_all) plus a RegexBuilder with jit(true), optimize_prefixes, size_limit, nest_limit and backtrack_limit, and try_* methods that report an exhausted backtracking budget instead of a silent no-match.
how_it_is_fast: Picks one of several engines per pattern: bit-parallel Shift-Or for small NFAs (64 states or fewer), lazy and eager DFAs, a PikeVM, a tagged NFA and a one-pass capture engine for captures, and a budgeted backtracker for backreferences. With the jit feature, the DFA, Shift-Or, tagged NFA, one-pass and backtracking engines are emitted as native code through dynasm. Literal prefilters (memchr, a custom AVX2 Teddy for 2-8 literals, aho-corasick for larger sets, NEON on AArch64 since 0.3.2) skip to candidate positions, and optimize_prefixes merges large literal alternations into a trie.
when_to_use: Rust tokenizer or pre-tokenizer code that runs GPT-style split patterns with lookaheads such as \s+(?!\S), where the regex crate refuses the pattern and fancy-regex has no JIT.
You want PCRE-like features (lookaround, backreferences, \X grapheme clusters) with only a cargo dependency, including on wasm32 (interpreted engines only there).
Hot capture-heavy patterns over ASCII data where you would otherwise write ASCII classes for the regex crate anyway; enable features = ["full"] and jit(true) and measure.
You need backreference searches to stop under a step budget (backtrack_limit, try_find) rather than hang.
when_not_to_use: General-purpose matching: the README itself says to use the regex crate for 99% of uses, and the non-JIT engine is 0.80-0.87x of regex on log_parsing, url_extraction and html_tags in its own table.
Code that relies on Unicode \w, \d or \b: regexr makes them ASCII-only unless you add (?u), unlike the regex crate, so the same pattern string silently matches less on non-ASCII text.

Correctness-critical use where match semantics must equal the regex crate or PCRE2: every release from 0.2 to 0.6.0 (2026-09-28) fixed wrong-match bugs (DFA longest-instead-of-leftmost-first, JIT DFA giving up early, lazy-DFA cache flush dropping matches, lookbehind errors).
Short-lived regexes matched a few times: JIT compile cost is not amortized (the docs say so), and patterns with large Unicode classes do better on the lazy DFA than the JIT.
Possessive quantifiers, atomic groups or variable-width lookbehind are needed: they are rejected or only fixed-width is supported.

integration.dependencies: memchr 2.8, aho-corasick 1.1; optional dynasm and dynasmrt 5.1 for the jit feature (no C library)
integration.platforms: any Rust target for the interpreted engines including wasm32-unknown-unknown; JIT on x86-64 (Linux, macOS, Windows) and AArch64 (Linux, macOS); AVX2 prefilters on x86-64, NEON literal prefilter on AArch64
integration.thread_safety: Regex is shareable across threads: lazy state sits behind RwLock (docs/architecture.md), and 0.5.0 stopped concurrent searches on one Regex from serializing on a shared lazy DFA.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: method names and Match/Captures types follow the regex crate, but \w, \d and \b default to ASCII, backtracking for backreferences is budgeted, possessive and atomic groups are rejected, and the crate is a different type, so it is a code change, not a Cargo swap

gotchas: Harness flaw behind the headline: benches/competitors.rs passes the same pattern string to every engine, but regexr (and the pcre2 crate without UTF/UCP) treat \d, \w and \b as ASCII while the regex crate treats them as Unicode (\w is about 140,000 codepoints; the regex docs recommend (?-u:\w) when ASCII suffices). The 3.91-4.09x log_parsing row ((\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}) ... \[(\w+)\] (.+)) therefore compares ASCII regexr against Unicode regex, and on unicode_letters regexr's \w+ skips the Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic, Hebrew and Greek words the regex crate matches, so the engines produce different results. The harness never checks that match counts agree.

The README table has not changed since the initial commit (2025-12-01): the alternation row was timed on log data that, by the current test_data.rs's own comment, contained no lowercase error/warning/critical/fatal at all (a rejection scan, not a search), and all rows predate the 0.1.x to 0.6.0 correctness fixes, several of which moved patterns to different engines.
Results are not committed (benches/results is gitignored) and no CPU, rustc or PCRE2 version is given; criterion runs use sample_size 10, 1 s measurement and inputs of only 1 KB to 100 KB.
docs/features.md lists \w as [a-zA-Z0-9_] in one section and shows \w+ matching 'café' as 'Unicode word characters' in another; the source (src/hir/builder.rs) gates Unicode \w, \d and \b on (?u).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick regexr when you are in Rust, need lookarounds or backreferences in a tokenizer pattern and cannot link PCRE2; for plain throughput on Rust the regex crate stays the default, and for large multi-pattern rule sets Hyperscan, or for RE2-semantics engines rejit and re2jit, are the better-measured choices.
verified_claims_summary: First-party criterion runs (regex 1.13, pcre2 crate 0.2, fancy-regex 0.19; CPU, rustc and PCRE2 version not stated) report regexr-jit at 3.91-4.09x the regex crate on log parsing and 1.33-1.99x on HTML tag and URL extraction, with pcre2-jit faster on URLs and Unicode text; the log-parsing and Unicode rows compare ASCII regexr against Unicode regex, and the table dates from the 2025-12 initial commit.
status_note: Actively maintained (0.6.0 released 2026-09-28, about 36k crates.io downloads, MIT OR Apache-2.0), but the match engine is still settling: each recent release fixes wrong-match bugs, and the only published speed numbers are an undated pre-0.1 table with a semantic mismatch on its headline row.
